extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples drawn from 31 source datasets, including 736 newly curated examples from IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MathVista was compiled from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). The authors collected MathQA datasets in multimodal settings, reviewed more than 70 VQA datasets and selected 19 publicly available datasets with math-related instances, and manually annotated the three new datasets. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select likely mathematical examples, followed by manual labeling by expert annotators and majority voting.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 85.6% of examples have annotations; the paper notes that annotations were sourced from original data providers and that some examples lacked annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Existing multimodal MathQA and VQA datasets, plus newly sourced questions from puzzle test figures, functional plots, and academic paper figures. PaperQA examples were sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely involving mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates, then three expert annotators manually labeled them. Majority voting was used to finalize labels, and each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. The final dataset was split into testmini and test, with testmini sampled to closely match the overall distribution.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Examples with numeric answers or quantity words were selected for automatic filtration. False positives were removed through manual labeling. Source datasets were capped at 400 examples each. The final benchmark was normalized into multiple-choice and free-form answer formats, and free-form answers were standardized as integers, floating numbers, or lists.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: New questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. For mathematical reasoning labeling, three reviewers independently annotated each example, disagreements were resolved through discussion, and majority voting was used for final labels. For newly collected questions, the paper reports 99.2% inter-annotation consistency and only 6 disagreements among 736 questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom annotation tool GUI shown in the paper; Amazon Mechanical Turk was used for human performance evaluation and Bard assessment tasks, not for the main dataset annotation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For the newly collected questions, three reviewers independently annotated each dataset, disagreements were resolved by discussion, and majority voting was used. For mathematical reasoning labels, the paper reports 94.1% exact set agreement and 98.79% individual label agreement between automatic and human annotations, and a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 for annotator agreement on problem labeling.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 for the newly collected questions and mathematical reasoning labeling; 5 annotators per question were used for the human performance evaluation subset.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields for dataset annotation; human performance annotators were required to have a high school diploma or higher, a history of more than 5,000 HIT tasks, and an acceptance score higher than 0.99.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used as an answer extractor for evaluation; EasyOCR was used to detect OCR text; Multimodal Bard was used to generate image captions; automatic heuristic rules were used to select likely mathematical questions.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is split into testmini and test; answer labels for test are not publicly released to prevent contamination. The authors state they will maintain an online evaluation platform and continue refining the dataset and leaderboard in response to community feedback and new models.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language, grade level, and educational attainment of annotators were collected or used in the benchmark context; the dataset also includes questions involving age and geography in examples, but these are not described as collected personal attributes.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to support development of general-purpose AI agents for mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, including educational, analytical, theorem-proving, and scientific applications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that source datasets are heterogeneous and that annotations lack a unified format and structure. It also reports that the benchmark includes 6.57% non-English questions, which may affect model performance across languages.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Coverage gaps remain for certain mathematical problems and visual contexts. The benchmark is labor-intensive to curate, has heterogeneous annotations, and is not fully annotated (only 85.6% of examples have annotations). The test labels are withheld to avoid contamination. The authors also note that the benchmark may not generalize broadly to other domains.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking, validation, and standard evaluation of foundation models for mathematical reasoning in visual contexts. testmini is intended for model development validation or limited-compute settings, while test is intended for standard evaluation.
